title: Black Hawk Helicopter Repairer Discusses Wildfire Mission
description:
Army Staff Sgt. Carlos Araujo, assigned to the California Army National Guard's 40th Combat Aviation Brigade, discusses the unit’s joint operations with the California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection, or Cal Fire, to battle Los Angeles County fires. The California National Guard activated more than 800 service members to help law enforcement and emergency services fight fires raging across the county.

Video by Army National Guard Spc. William Franco Espinosa
keywords: california army national guard, 40th Combat Aviation Brigade, DGOV, Featured Video, Defense on Demand

transcript.text: Well , my name is Staff Sergeant Carlos
Sarajo . I'm a 15 Tango , which is a
Black Hawk helicopter repair . So the
40th cab was activated , uh , because
of the state of emergency . Once we get
the state of emergency , it's very
quick to activate us , and , uh , the
whole reason we got launched is because
of the Palisades fires , the Eaton
fires , all those people that are in
danger . As a crew chief for the Black
Hawk , uh , our primary role here is to
be able to move passengers or evacuate
anybody who's in danger . Uh , we can
also move fire crews from one point to
another on any of the rocky terrain or
the difficult to access terrain . We
also have the water dropping . Which is
what they see the most , and we're able
to take water from small ponds ,
reservoirs , creeks , whatever they

to go out there and put the wet stuff
on the hot stuff and slow it down so
the firefighters on the ground can
really put in some fight . Working with
Cal Fire on a mission like this is
incredible . They integrate with us
just as if they were military the
entire time . So working with them is
basically like having two of us in
there instead of just one of us back
there being able to do everything , you
have another guy over there . Every bit
of confidence in them being able to do
exactly what we do , just to everybody ,
um , the guard is here to help . Just
know we're doing our absolute best to
do it and to make sure that we're doing
everything we can to protect lives and
property as fast as we can and as
safely as we can .
